estimates from a fit to the same data model <- data.frame(sex = rep(c("female", "male"), each = 3),     type = "parameter", form = "exponential",     parameter = c("nugget", "partial.sill", "timescale"),     estimate = c(0.0059, 0.189, 1.00, 0, 0.294, 2.30),     min.lag = 0.2, max.lag = 8.2) plotLagProfile(tse, name = "variogram_sex", model = model)   # Hourly samples with reads of four vessels of an artificial gut, hours # 476 to 592, one sample per hour, and the five most abundant taxa data("SilvermanAGutData", package = "miaTime") tse <- SilvermanAGutData tse <- tse[, tse$SampleType == "Hourly" &     tse$Normal_Noise_Sample == "Normal" & tse$Time.hr %in% 476:592 &     colSums(SummarizedExperiment::assay(tse)) > 0] tse <- tse[, !duplicated(paste(tse$Vessel, tse$Time.hr))] tse <- mia::transformAssay(tse, method = "relabundance") tse <- tse[mia::getTop(tse, top = 5), ]  # Illustrative autocorrelation table in the form of miaTime's # getAutocorrelation(), from stats::acf() on the hourly grid; hours # without a sample are NA acfs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(tse$Vessel), function(v) {     j <- match(476:592, tse$Time.hr[tse$Vessel == v])     m <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(tse, "relabundance")[,         tse$Vessel == v][, j]     present <- !is.na(j)     do.call(rbind, lapply(rownames(m), function(feature) {         r <- stats::acf(m[feature, ], lag.max = 12,             na.action = stats::na.pass, plot = FALSE)         data.frame(FeatureID = feature, Vessel = v, lag = 1:12,             acf = r$acf[-1L], n.pairs = vapply(1:12, function(l)                 sum(present[-seq_len(l)] & head(present, -l)),                 integer(1)))     })) })) plotLagProfile(acfs, group = "Vessel", colour.by = "FeatureID")

code: # Correlations above 0.4 between 15 genera, in women and men data("hitchip1006", package = "miaTime") tse <- hitchip1006[, hitchip1006$time == 0 & !is.na(hitchip1006$sex)] tse <- mia::transformAssay(tse, method = "clr", pseudocount = 1) top <- names(sort(rowMeans(SummarizedExperiment::assay(tse, "counts")),     decreasing = TRUE))[1:15] edges <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("female", "male"), function(s) {     r <- cor(t(SummarizedExperiment::assay(tse, "clr")[top,         tse$sex == s]))     i <- which(abs(r) > 0.4 & upper.tri(r), arr.ind = TRUE)     data.frame(from = top[i[, 1]], to = top[i[, 2]], weight = r[i],         sex = s) })) S4Vectors::metadata(tse)$correlations <- edges plotNetwork(tse, edges = "correlations", split.by = "sex")   # Edges gained and lost from women to men plotNetwork(tse, edges = "correlations", split.by = "sex", diff = TRUE)   # All correlations as a matrix, with FDR q-values below 0.05 marked pairs <- t(combn(top, 2)) edges <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("female", "male"), function(s) {     m <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(tse, "clr")[, tse$sex == s]     test <- apply(pairs, 1, function(p) cor.test(m[p[1], ], m[p[2], ]))     data.frame(from = pairs[, 1], to = pairs[, 2], sex = s,         weight = vapply(test, `[[`, numeric(1), "estimate"),         p = vapply(test, `[[`, numeric(1), "p.value")) })) edges$q <- p.adjust(edges$p, method = "fdr") S4Vectors::metadata(tse)$all <- edges plotNetwork(tse, edges = "all", split.by = "sex", layout = "matrix",     p.col = "q")   # Moves between the dominant genera of consecutive samples tse <- mia::addDominant(hitchip1006, name = "dominant") cd <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(tse)) cd <- cd[order(cd$subject, cd$time), ] n <- nrow(cd) same <- cd$subject[-1] == cd$subject[-n] moves <- data.frame(from = cd$dominant[-n][same],     to = cd$dominant[-1][same], weight = 1) moves <- aggregate(weight ~ from + to, data = moves, FUN = sum) S4Vectors::metadata(tse)$moves <- moves plotNetwork(tse, edges = "moves", directed = TRUE)
